verses.text: This was the land assigned by lot to the tribe of Manasseh, Joseph's firstborn. Machir, Manasseh's firstborn and the father of Gilead, received Gilead and Bashan because he was a warrior.
Land also went to the rest of Manasseh's descendants, clan by clan: Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida. These were the clans descended from the sons of Manasseh son of Joseph.
Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, had daughters but no sons. His daughters were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

They came before Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders. They said, “The LORD told Moses to give us an inheritance alongside our brothers.” So Joshua gave them an inheritance among their father's brothers, just as the LORD had commanded.
Manasseh received ten shares in addition to Gilead and Bashan east of the Jordan.
That's because Manasseh's daughters received an inheritance alongside his sons. The rest of Manasseh's sons received Gilead.
Manasseh's border ran from Asher to Michmethath, near Shechem. From there it turned to the right toward the people of En Tappuah.
The land around Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, but the town of Tappuah on Manasseh's border belonged to Ephraim.
The border went down to the Kanah Brook. On the south side of the brook were Ephraim's towns among the towns of Manasseh. Manasseh's border ran along the north side of the brook and ended at the sea.
The land to the south belonged to Ephraim and the land to the north to Manasseh, with the sea marking Manasseh's boundary. Manasseh's territory reached Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.
Within Issachar and Asher, Manasseh received Beth Shean and Ibleam with their towns, and the people of Dor, Endor, Taanach, and Megiddo with their towns. This included three hill districts.
The people of Manasseh couldn't drive out the people of those towns. The Canaanites were determined to stay in that land.
When the Israelites grew stronger, they made the Canaanites do forced labor, but they never drove them out completely.
Joseph's descendants asked Joshua, “Why have you given us only one allotment, one share of land? There are so many of us because the LORD has blessed us all this time.”
Joshua said, “If there are so many of you and Ephraim's hill country is too small, go into the forest in the territory of the Perizzites and Rephaim and clear land there for yourselves.”

Joseph's descendants said, “The hill country isn't enough for us. And all the Canaanites in the valley have iron chariots, both the ones in Beth Shean and its towns and the ones in the Valley of Jezreel.”
Joshua told the house of Joseph, Ephraim and Manasseh, “There are many of you, and you're strong. You'll have more than one share.
The hill country will be yours. It's forest now, but you'll clear it, and it'll be yours to its farthest edge. You'll drive the Canaanites out, even though they have iron chariots and are strong.”
